fact_text: Debt-to-equity ratio equals total debt, meaning short-term and long-term loans and other borrowings from the liabilities side of the balance sheet, divided by total shareholders' equity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: A debt-to-equity ratio of 1 means each rupee of owner funding is matched by one rupee of borrowing, while 0.2 means only 20 paisa of debt stands behind each rupee of equity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst treats a debt-to-equity ratio near 50 percent as a comfortable benchmark for most businesses, zero or below as the safest, and above 100 percent as a sign of possible solvency pressure.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Only interest-bearing borrowings count as debt; trade payables, unclaimed dividends and deferred liabilities sit under liabilities but are excluded from the debt figure in this ratio.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: A negative debt-to-equity ratio appears when accumulated losses push shareholders' equity below zero, leaving owners with almost no equity cushion; the analyst ruled such companies out for investment.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst says a debt-to-equity screen should be read alongside profitability and other solvency ratios, comparing four or five companies together before choosing a stock.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Pakistan Petroleum is an exploration and production company that drills wells to extract oil and gas, and it must restore the land to its earlier condition after exploration under government requirements.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Pakistan Petroleum holds a decommissioning provision of about 4,927 crore rupees to dismantle rigs and restore land later; it is a liability but is not counted as debt.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Pakistan Petroleum's non-current long-term financing is about 109 crore rupees, a very small borrowing for the company.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: About 13 crore rupees of Pakistan Petroleum's long-term financing matures in the current year and is included in its current liabilities as debt.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Adding non-current and current borrowings, Pakistan Petroleum's total debt comes to about 122 crore rupees, which the analyst calls small for a company of its size.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Pakistan Petroleum's debt-to-equity ratio works out to about 0.0018 times, meaning very little borrowing behind each rupee of shareholder equity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst describes Pakistan Petroleum as cash rich, so it has little need to borrow, while noting that borrowing is not a negative for companies that use it to expand.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: World Call Telecom shows a debt-to-equity ratio of about minus 205 percent because its shareholders' equity has turned negative.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Silk's debt-to-equity ratio is about minus 4,000 percent, which the analyst attributes to continuous losses, heavy debt and weak earnings leaving negative equity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst lists PACE among loss-making companies whose retained earnings and equity have turned negative, so their debt-to-equity ratio gives no useful investment signal.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Abbott Laboratories Pakistan has the lowest debt-to-equity ratio in the pharma group the analyst compared, at about 0.37 times, which he regards as very good.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: For pharma companies the analyst treats a debt-to-equity ratio around 50 percent as ideal, and views a high ratio in the sector negatively.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: About 25 percent of CPHL's assets are financed by debt, which the analyst links to research and development on new products and active pharmaceutical ingredients.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst says technology companies should keep debt-to-equity very low, ideally under 10 percent, because they need little production capacity and usually fund growth with equity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Technology start-ups are expected to raise equity rather than borrow, so the analyst treats heavy debt in a tech company as a red flag.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: The analyst calls Hum Network a good technology company on leverage, with low borrowing, and says Avanceon (AVN) also carries little debt relative to its peers.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Debt-to-equity is not a useful screen for banks, because deposit and borrowing funded models push ratios to roughly 1,200 to 1,400 percent for banks such as FABL, ABL, HBL and BIPL.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)

fact_text: Gas utility SSGC shows a very high debt-to-equity ratio, but the analyst says its essential service and monopoly position make the ratio easier to accept than in other sectors.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Debt to Equity Ratio Explained: PSX Stock Analysis & Company Insights | Pakistan Stock Market Tips' (YouTube, 2025-01-11)
